newsitem.title: USA: Netanyahu defends Orthodox conversion law.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu defends Orthodox conversion law.

text.p: Reform and Conservative American Jewish leaders called on Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Monday to oppose legislation in the Knesset that would endorse conversions only if performed by Orthodox rabbis.

Reform and Conservative leaders, who represent about 90 percent of some six million Jews in the United States, scheduled an hour-long meeting with Netanyahu at his hotel here during a whirlwind Washington visit before he was to return to Israel.

Netanyahu has refused to block legislation that would invalidate conversions to Judaism if they are performed by non-Orthodox rabbis. It passed the first of three readings in the Knesset, the Israeli parliament, last week. Ultra-Orthodox politicians in Israel shore up Netanyahu's ruling coalition.
Netanyahu told a press conference that it was not true the legislation would invalidate conversions done abroad by Reform or Conservative rabbis, only within Israel.
"The proposed legislation in Israel doesn't alter anything," he insisted.
"This whole process has been undertaken because of litigation" by Reform and Conservative Jews to challenge the status quo in Israel that gave Orthodox rabbis greater authority.
"I think someone should try and get that Genie back in the bottle," he said, suggesting that if the lawsuits were dropped, the legislation would not be needed.
Rabbi Eric Yoffie, president of the Union of American Hebrew Congregations, called the results of a meeting with Netanyahu on the conversion issue in New York in February "negative."

He said before Monday's meeting that "the prime minister did not do much to address our concerns that as the leader of the Jewish people he must be a unifying force in Jewish life, speaking for all Jews, of all denominations."
Netanyahu cancelled a scheduled speech on Sunday night to 500 Reform Jewish leaders, citing a scheduling conflict.
